headline: Democratic Governors Group Spends $4.3M to Shield Hochul From Blakeman Surge
blurb: The Democratic Governors Association is putting $4.3 million behind Gov. Hochul as Republican Bruce Blakeman gains ground.

headline: Manhunt Continues for Gunman in Deadly Midtown Subway Shooting
blurb: The NYPD is still searching for the man who shot a 26-year-old rider dead on the 7th Avenue–53rd Street platform Saturday, and has added patrols in Midtown stations.

headline: Mahmoud Khalil Asks Supreme Court to Let Judges Quickly Reverse Immigration Detentions
blurb: Activist Mahmoud Khalil, a green-card holder detained last year over his role in pro-Palestinian protests, asked the Supreme Court to let federal judges quickly reverse immigration detentions.

headline: City's 2-K Child Care Program to Expand to Every Borough Next Fall
blurb: Mayor Mamdani and Gov. Hochul announced that free 2-K will reach every borough next fall, growing from about 2,000 seats this year to more than 12,000.

headline: Wrong-Way Driver Dead, Four Hurt in West Shore Expressway Pileup
blurb: A 66-year-old woman died when her Kia collided with a Range Rover traveling the wrong way on the West Shore Expressway. Four other people were hurt.

headline: Mamdani Replaces Four Members of NYPD Civilian Watchdog Board
blurb: The mayor replaced four members of the Civilian Complaint Review Board, the agency that investigates police misconduct.

headline: Blakeman Calls Hochul a 'Useful Tool' Who Takes Orders From Mamdani
blurb: Republican candidate Bruce Blakeman attacked Gov. Hochul as taking direction from Mayor Mamdani in the final weeks of the governor's race.

headline: 1tbsp Plays All Night at Nowadays Oct. 22
blurb: Nowadays hands the decks to 1tbsp for an all-night set on Thursday, Oct. 22.

headline: Nowadays Nonstop Runs Oct. 24 With Ayesha, Mor Elian and Pearson Sound
blurb: The club's marathon Nonstop party on Saturday, Oct. 24 features Ayesha, Mor Elian, Baby Leo, BEARCAT, Pearson Sound, Tasha, The Untouchables and more.

headline: Mister Sunday Brings Floating Points and Justin Carter to Nowadays Oct. 25
blurb: The long-running Mister Sunday party hosts Floating Points alongside resident Justin Carter on Sunday, Oct. 25.

headline: Hercules & Love Affair, Dustin Zahn and Eli Escobar Play BASEMENT Oct. 24
blurb: BASEMENT's Saturday, Oct. 24 lineup includes Dustin Zahn, Kameliia, Ade Kassim, Hercules & Love Affair, Eli Escobar and Andi.

headline: FIST Takes Over BASEMENT Friday, Oct. 23
blurb: The FIST party lands at BASEMENT on Oct. 23 with Lacchesi, Nene H, Word of Command, DJ Clone, Jubilee, Mez Monty and Connor Wrong.

headline: House Legend Ultra Naté Headlines Paradiso at Paragon Oct. 23
blurb: Paragon's Paradiso night on Friday, Oct. 23 features Ultra Naté with Kilopatrah Jones, Karim Olen Ash, Saia and RATONC1T0.

headline: Effy Plays H0L0 Friday, Oct. 23
blurb: Ridgewood club H0L0 books Effy for its Friday, Oct. 23 night.

headline: Superior Ingredients Hosts 'A Day in Tulum' Music and Arts Festival Oct. 25
blurb: Superior Ingredients stages A Day in Tulum, a daytime music and arts festival, on Sunday, Oct. 25.

headline: Floating Points Headlines Refuge Saturday Oct. 24
blurb: Refuge's Saturday party on Oct. 24 features Floating Points, starting at 10 p.m. The club marked its first anniversary in September with a 72-hour party.

headline: Victor Calderone Leads Refuge's Halloween Morning Marathon Oct. 31
blurb: Refuge opens a Halloween Saturday morning marathon at 6 a.m. on Oct. 31 with Victor Calderone.

headline: L7 Brings 'Last Hurrah' Tour to Knockdown Center Oct. 24
blurb: Los Angeles rock band L7 plays Knockdown Center on Saturday, Oct. 24 on what it calls The Last Hurrah Tour. Tickets start at $51.

headline: Helado Negro and Reyna Tropical Team Up for 'Helado Tropical' at Knockdown Oct. 25
blurb: Helado Negro and Reyna Tropical present a joint night, Helado Tropical, at Knockdown Center on Sunday, Oct. 25. Tickets from $38.

headline: Circoloco Halloween Weekend Sells Out Brooklyn Storehouse
blurb: Teksupport's two-night Circoloco Halloween at Brooklyn Storehouse on Oct. 30 and 31 is listed as sold out, with tickets that started at $182. The Navy Yard venue has announced it is shutting down.

headline: Kaytranada Plays Pacha NYC Halloween Eve
blurb: Kaytranada headlines Pacha NYC on Friday, Oct. 30 at 10 p.m., with tickets from $222.

headline: Purple Disco Machine Takes Halloween Night at Pacha NYC
blurb: German producer Purple Disco Machine plays Pacha NYC on Saturday, Oct. 31. Tickets from $133.

headline: Lost Frequencies at Marquee New York Oct. 30
blurb: Belgian DJ Lost Frequencies plays Marquee New York on Oct. 30 at 11 p.m. 21+, with tables or general admission.

headline: Two Friends Close Out Halloween at Marquee
blurb: The DJ duo Two Friends headline Marquee New York on Halloween night, Oct. 31, at 11 p.m. 21+.

headline: TWA Hotel Throws Three-Day 'Mission: 60s' Space-Age Party
blurb: The TWA Hotel at JFK is staging a three-day retro space weekend with real astronauts, a Star Trek actor and a field trip to a rocket park.

headline: Venetian Wine Bar Bicchiere Opens Second Upper East Side Location
blurb: Bicchiere has opened a second Upper East Side wine bar in the former Madame Bonte Café space, serving seven styles of house-made bigoli.

headline: Greenpoint Luxury Tower Ran on Generator for a Month After Fire; Tenants Sue
blurb: Residents of The Greenpoint, paying up to $12,000 a month, lived for weeks on generator power after a fire. One tenant has sued in housing court.

headline: MTA Watchdog: Bronx Subway Shop Roofs Endanger Crews, Crane Leak Ran 15 Years
blurb: An MTA inspector general report found water leaking onto crane equipment for 15 years at an East 180th Street repair shop and falling concrete at another Bronx shop.

headline: Blakeman Uses Fatal Subway Shooting as Campaign Cudgel Against Hochul
blurb: Republican Bruce Blakeman seized on the deadly Midtown subway shooting to attack Gov. Hochul, whose campaign pointed to state money she has steered to NYPD subway overtime.

headline: Queens Officers Revive Infant in Frantic CPR Rescue
blurb: Two NYPD officers answering a call in Astoria performed CPR on a 1-month-old boy who was not breathing and had no pulse, saving his life.

headline: Investigation Details Hourslong Ordeal for Six Nonverbal Students on School Bus
blurb: Six students ages 6 to 8, all nonverbal with special needs, reached school more than four hours late after their bus went off route, an investigation found.

headline: Brooklyn Conservatory of Music Opens Second Campus
blurb: The Brooklyn Conservatory of Music has opened a second campus, NY1 reported.

headline: Santos Bravos Marks First Anniversary at K-Pop Nara Ahead of NYC Debut
blurb: Santos Bravos, billed as the voice of a new Latin generation, celebrated its first anniversary with fans at K-Pop Nara ahead of the group's New York debut.

headline: One Dead, One Hurt in Park Hill Avenue Fire on Block With History of Blazes
blurb: A Saturday-night fire in a Staten Island apartment building on Park Hill Avenue killed one person and injured another. The block has seen repeated fires in recent years.

headline: Queens Father Sues NYPD, Says Cops Rammed Moped Carrying His 14-Year-Old
blurb: A federal lawsuit says officers crossed a double yellow line and struck a moped carrying a 14-year-old in Corona. The teen suffered a broken femur and was handcuffed while being loaded into an ambulance, the suit says.

headline: Vacate Order Issued After Crash Into Howard Beach Pizzeria
blurb: A building was ordered vacated after a vehicle slammed into a Howard Beach pizzeria.

headline: Natalie Maines Mocks Trump at Beacon Theatre; White House Fires Back
blurb: At a Beacon Theatre show, the Chicks singer took a jab at President Trump, saying she would now kiss George W. Bush. The White House responded by calling her a despicable nobody.

headline: Bloomberg-Backed Charter PAC Pours $1.8M Into Hochul Reelection Push
blurb: A charter school political action committee backed by Michael Bloomberg has put $1.8 million behind Gov. Hochul's campaign.

headline: New Charges Filed in FIT Student's Fentanyl Death
blurb: Prosecutors brought new charges in the March fentanyl death of a Fashion Institute of Technology student, officials said.

headline: Mamdani Asks Parking Lot and Garage Owners to Deny ICE Access
blurb: Following the Oct. 8 Marble Hill shooting, the mayor asked private parking lot and garage operators to refuse access to immigration agents. Elected officials separately urged Target to stop ICE use of its Marble Hill lot.

headline: Lawyers Say ICE Officer Fired Into New Yorker's Car Without Warning
blurb: Attorneys for the 28-year-old shot by an immigration officer in Marble Hill on Oct. 8 allege the officer broke his car window and fired without identifying himself.

headline: Mamdani Cuts Ad Backing Hochul's Reelection
blurb: Mayor Mamdani released an ad backing Gov. Hochul that also criticized Republican Bruce Blakeman for opposing universal child care.

headline: Queens Officials Renew Calls to Abolish ICE After Marble Hill Shooting
blurb: Assembly Member Jessica González-Rojas and Council Member Julie Won renewed calls to abolish ICE after agents shot a 28-year-old man in Marble Hill with his young son in the car. Won also urged the mayor to fire Commissioner Tisch; Republican Council Member Joann Ariola dismissed the abolition push.

headline: Hochul Backs Mamdani's Decision to Keep Tisch as Police Commissioner
blurb: Gov. Hochul called it a smart decision that Mayor Mamdani refused to fire NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch despite pressure from the Democratic Socialists of America.

headline: Plaza Hotel to Close in January for Four-Year Renovation
blurb: The Plaza's last day of service is set for Jan. 19, with renovation work starting the next day, according to a report.

headline: Maduro Calls New Torture Allegations 'False' in Manhattan Federal Court
blurb: Former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro, held in New York since January, denied torture allegations in a new federal indictment and twice refused a judge's request to enter a plea.

headline: Comptroller Levine Walks Back Pledge to Buy Israel Bonds
blurb: City Comptroller Mark Levine is abandoning a campaign promise to invest city pension money in Israel bonds, according to The New York Times.

headline: 50 Years of Punk: Manic Panic Founders Spotlighted in New Exhibit
blurb: A new exhibit honors the two Bronx sisters who opened the nation's first punk rock boutique, Manic Panic, in 1977.

headline: Mamdani Stands By NYPD Commissioner Amid Calls for Removal After ICE Shooting
blurb: Mayor Zohran Mamdani stood by Commissioner Jessica Tisch despite calls for her removal after the federal agent shooting in Marble Hill, and announced a review of the ICE incident.

headline: Two Men Plead Not Guilty in Stabbing and Robbery of Off-Duty NYPD Detective
blurb: Two men accused of stabbing and robbing an off-duty NYPD detective in the Bronx, then hiding in Massachusetts, pleaded not guilty.

headline: Bronx Vigil Honors Young Mother Allegedly Pushed From Balcony
blurb: Neighbors gathered to remember a young mother who police say was pushed from a high-rise balcony by an ex-boyfriend, who has been charged in her death.

headline: Mayor and Council Speaker Agree to End Horse Carriage Industry
blurb: Mayor Mamdani and Council Speaker Julie Menin reached a deal to ban horse-drawn carriages, with job training for drivers and a full ban in 2028. Drivers and the Transport Workers Union rallied against it Oct. 16 ahead of a Council vote.

headline: Hochul and Blakeman Clash in Governor's Debate
blurb: Gov. Kathy Hochul and Republican challenger Bruce Blakeman sparred in a televised gubernatorial debate ahead of the Nov. 3 election.

headline: Off-Duty NYPD Detective Who Was Stabbed and Robbed Speaks Out
blurb: The off-duty detective stabbed and robbed in the Bronx earlier this month spoke publicly for the first time after his release from the hospital.

headline: Soho House Plans Fourth NYC Club in NoMad's Johnston Building
blurb: Soho House will open its fourth New York clubhouse in early 2028 in the 1903 Johnston Building at Broadway and West 28th Street, with a 20,000-square-foot health club, sharing the building with The Ned NoMad.

headline: Mamdani Launches 'Debt Demolisher' Relief Program for Unpaid City Fines
blurb: The city's new debt relief program for unpaid fines is projected to recover $25 million that might otherwise go uncollected.

headline: Mamdani Orders NYPD Review of Use-of-Force Policies After Teen's Death
blurb: The mayor directed the NYPD to review its use-of-force policies after the case of Win Rozario, the 19-year-old police fatally shot in his Queens home during a mental health crisis after he called 911.

headline: Mamdani Faces Accountability Assembly on Housing and NYCHA Repairs
blurb: The mayor met clergy and community leaders at Queens College for an accountability assembly on housing and NYCHA repairs organized by Metro IAF.

headline: Videos Show Marble Hill ICE Shooting Unfolded in Seconds
blurb: Videos show the Marble Hill shooting, in which a 28-year-old driver was shot in the neck with a 5-year-old in the car, unfolded in a few chaotic seconds. Officials say the officers believed they were in danger.

headline: Mamdani Orders Use-of-Force Review After Officer in Win Rozario Shooting Retires
blurb: Mayor Mamdani ordered an NYPD review of use-of-force rules and accountability reforms after the officer involved in the fatal police shooting of teenager Win Rozario retired before his disciplinary trial.

headline: Marble Hill Detainee Still Has Bullet in His Neck, Attorneys Say
blurb: Lawyers for the man shot by ICE agents in Marble Hill say he still has a bullet lodged in his neck and has not eaten while in federal custody. Protesters rallied for ICE to leave the city.

headline: Gowanus Open Studios Turns 30 as Rising Rents Squeeze Artists Out
blurb: The neighborhood's open studios weekend marked its 30th year even as climbing rents push working artists out of Gowanus.

headline: Arturo O'Farrill Brings Afro Latin Jazz to Harlem
blurb: Bandleader Arturo O'Farrill talked with NY1 about bringing his Afro Latin jazz to Harlem.

headline: Mamdani Says ICE Agent Looked Like a 'Mass Shooter' at Marble Hill Stop
blurb: The mayor described the federal agent who opened fire during a Marble Hill traffic stop as looking like a mass shooter.

headline: Mamdani Says Talks With Trump Failed to Free Man Shot by ICE Agents
blurb: The mayor said his talks with President Trump did not win the release of the man wounded when federal agents fired seven shots in Marble Hill.

headline: Manhattan Prosecutors Push to Keep State Case Against Mangione Alive
blurb: New York prosecutors are seeking to sustain their murder case against Luigi Mangione despite his plea in the federal case.

headline: Homeland Security Secretary Offers Murky Account of Marble Hill Shooting
blurb: Homeland Security Secretary Mullin gave an unclear account of the ICE shooting and made false claims about Mayor Mamdani, amNY reported.

headline: Judges Hear 9/11 Families' Case Against Saudi Arabia
blurb: Judges heard arguments in the long-running lawsuit by Sept. 11 families who argue the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia helped the attackers.

headline: Pro-Palestinian Protesters Disrupt Oct. 7 Vigil, Heckle Mamdani
blurb: Protesters crashed an Oct. 7 memorial vigil and jeered Mayor Mamdani as a traitor.

headline: James and Komatireddy Trade Blows in Attorney General Debate
blurb: Attorney General Letitia James called Republican challenger Saritha Komatireddy a Trump puppet in a fiery NY1 debate and defended her remarks on the Cornell rape case.

headline: Shuttered Cobble Hill Firehouse to Become $17.8M Noel Pointer Music Center
blurb: Work has begun on converting the former Engine 204 firehouse at 299 Degraw St., closed since 2003, into a home for the Noel Pointer Foundation's free music programs, with recording studios and a performance hall. Construction is expected to take about two years.

headline: Firefighter Killed in Brooklyn Blaze Honored at FDNY Memorial
blurb: A firefighter who died fighting a Brooklyn fire received posthumous honors at the FDNY's Upper Manhattan memorial.

headline: Court Orders Promoter Teksupport and Parent Firm to Cease Operations After Nov. 7
blurb: After months of legal disputes, a court ruled that long-running New York party series Teksupport must stop operating after Nov. 7. Its sold-out Circoloco Halloween weekend at Brooklyn Storehouse falls just before the deadline.

headline: NYC Crime Hits Historic Lows Through Nine Months, but Hate Crimes Rise
blurb: NYPD figures for the third quarter show overall crime continuing at historic lows, while reported hate crimes climbed.

headline: Staten Island Lands First Community Justice Center With $20 Million
blurb: Staten Island will get its first community justice center, backed by $20 million in combined funding.

headline: Ticketing Company Posh to Open Its First New York Venue
blurb: Nightlife ticketing app Posh is opening a brick-and-mortar New York venue, according to a job posting, as a prototype for a national chain. The space will host public and private events and be offered as a perk to top promoters. Name and location have not been announced.

headline: City Rent Freeze Takes Effect as Legal Fight Continues
blurb: The rent freeze on stabilized apartments took effect while a court challenge to it continues.

headline: City Unveils Plan to Combat Antisemitism
blurb: City officials announced a new plan to fight antisemitism as NYPD data show hate crimes rising.

headline: Federal Judge Strikes Down ICE Courthouse Arrest Policy Nationwide
blurb: A federal judge struck down the policy allowing immigration agents to make arrests at immigration courts across the country.

headline: Neir's Tavern Marks 197 Years With Free Block Party
blurb: Woodhaven's Neir's Tavern, among the city's oldest bars, threw a free 197th anniversary block party on Oct. 3 with music, food and drinks.

headline: Tokyo Record Bar Celebrates Thelonious Monk's 109th Birthday
blurb: Tokyo Record Bar on MacDougal Street hosted a three-night tribute Oct. 8-10 for Thelonious Monk's 109th birthday, curated by his grandchildren Sierre Monk and Thelonious IV Monk.

headline: Disco Tehran Celebrates Anniversary on Elsewhere Rooftop
blurb: The Disco Tehran party marked its anniversary with a 4-10 p.m. rooftop session at Elsewhere on Sunday, Oct. 4.

headline: Westside Cowboy Plays Music Hall of Williamsburg
blurb: Westside Cowboy played Music Hall of Williamsburg on Tuesday, Oct. 6.

headline: LCD Soundsystem Announces 12-Show Holiday Residency at Knockdown Center and Brooklyn Steel
blurb: LCD Soundsystem will return for its annual holiday New York residency, a 12-show run split between Knockdown Center and Brooklyn Steel that includes the band's 100th residency show.

headline: Federal Monitor Finds Nearly 10,000 NYPD Street Stops Missing From Records
blurb: The court-appointed monitor overseeing NYPD stop-and-frisk reforms reported that nearly 10,000 street stops were not recorded in department books.

headline: Brooklyn Commuter Dragged to Death by A Train After Bag Caught in Doors
blurb: A man was killed when his bag got caught in the doors of an A train and he was dragged along the platform.

headline: Woman Killed in Hit-and-Run While Biking on 34th Street
blurb: A cyclist was struck and killed on 34th Street in Midtown by a driver who fled.

headline: Bodycam Suggests Times Square Stabbing Suspect Wanted Police to Shoot Her
blurb: Newly released NYPD body camera video suggests the woman shot by police after stabbing two people in Times Square sought to be killed by officers.

headline: Over 100 Arrested at Netanyahu Protest; Councilman Chi Ossé Handcuffed
blurb: More than 100 people were arrested at a protest near the United Nations against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, including Councilman Chi Ossé. Mayor Mamdani did not join the march.

headline: Two-Alarm Bronx Fire Leaves One Dead, Another Hurt After Window Jump
blurb: One person died and another was injured after jumping from a window during a two-alarm fire in the Bronx.

headline: Loew's Paradise Theatre Roars Back as 4,000-Seat Arts Hub
blurb: The landmark Grand Concourse movie palace is being revived as a 4,000-seat performance and arts venue.
